S066-01.notes: 'So brittle that... reduced them to fragments' is the only cause-effect fit. Valuable/ancient are true but don't explain crumbling; legible contradicts the need for X-rays. Facts accurate (79 CE carbonization, 2023 scan of an unopened scroll).

S066-02.notes: A single touch doesn't close the trap, so the requirement filters out one-time stimuli. C is the trap, but enzymes come from later touches, not from the two-touch closing rule. B and D aren't supported. Facts accurate.

S066-03.notes: Only B compares 12 h with 24 h (78% vs 77%). C states the maximum but leaves out the 24 h value, so it doesn't show the lack of added benefit. A and D are about soaking vs. no soaking.

flags.note: D copies Text 2's finding almost word for word ('no more often than'), so the item becomes a matching exercise rather than a test of cross-text inference. Also, 'such events' in D has no antecedent inside the choice. Consider paraphrasing D, e.g. 'He would say the lines' directions do not show the astronomical alignment her argument requires.'

S066-04.notes: A, B and C aren't supported. C mixes up the later researchers with Hawkins and adds 'definitely'. Facts accurate (Reiche's calendar hypothesis; Hawkins's 1968 test found no more than chance alignment).

S066-05.notes: The text builds toward Glenn's distrust of the computer, Johnson checking it, and the flight going ahead. B overstates (the results matched). C is too broad and technical. D overstates the detail. Fact accurate (Glenn 1962).

S066-06.notes: The subject is 'the Terracotta Army' (singular), and it is separated from the verb by two modifiers. A is the plural trap from 'thousands'/'soldiers'. C and D leave the sentence without a main verb. Facts accurate.

S066-07.notes: Two independent clauses. A is a comma splice and B is a fused sentence. C turns the second part into a relative clause that is ungrammatical because 'she received the award for Annie Allen' already has a complete object structure. Facts accurate (1950 Pulitzer for Annie Allen; first Black Pulitzer winner).

S066-08.notes: The sentence adds another example of interests beyond spaceflight that matches the Peace Corps example, so 'Likewise' fits. There is no contrast with the previous sentence (rules out However), no causal link (Therefore) and no replacement (Instead). The trap is reading 'However' from 'after leaving NASA'. Facts accurate (Endeavour 1992; Sierra Leone/Liberia; left 1993; Jemison Group; Dartmouth).

S066-09.notes: Only D gives a reason why she was excluded. A, B and C are relevant background but don't explain it. The rules wording is accurate: before 1974 a deceased person could not be nominated (a posthumous award was possible only if the nomination came before death), and Franklin was never nominated. D leaves out 'never nominated' but is still accurate and sufficient.

S066-10.notes: Only B ties the discovery to the residents, who are descendants, and says why it mattered: it confirmed a history that had been hidden, matching the note that the ship was burned to hide evidence. A states the discovery but not why it mattered to residents. C and D are background. 'Hidden history' is an interpretive synthesis, but it is well grounded in the notes. 'Importing enslaved people... was outlawed' is accurate (1808); the importation was outlawed, not slavery.
